justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: R-01 via Real-Time Scoring Engine, R-02 via Case Management Backend and Fraud Analyst Frontend, and R-03 via Model Loader and Rule & Model Management Console, providing complete functional coverage.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Under 50 ms P99 at 3,000 TPS is well supported by Redis Feature Store pipelining, ONNX Runtime execution engine, DynamoDB Auto-Scaling, and asynchronous audit streaming via Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams.
justifications.compatibility: mTLS over gRPC/HTTP handles Payment Gateway integration and Card Networks / Token Vaults securely. However, the exact interface semantics and external contract details for external Token Vaults remain partially detailed.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analysts are well served by Fraud Analyst Frontend with Case Management Dashboard and real-time WebSocket updates. ML Engineers are supported via the Rule & Model Management Console and Model Loader.
justifications.reliability: Dead-Letter Queue, DynamoDB Streams, and ECS autoscaling ensure fault isolation. Context mentions fail-open fallback signals to Payment Gateways for R-07, though automated 1-minute failover/circuit-breaker execution mechanisms lack detailed component specifications.
justifications.security: PCI-DSS Level 1 is thoroughly addressed via AWS WAF, mTLS Validator, Client-Side Encryption Component, Audit Log Redactor, Audit Logging & Redaction Guard masking PANs, and S3 Object Lock for tamper-evident retention.
justifications.maintainability: Excellent modularity with clean separation between scoring, ML inference, and case management. Container and component boundaries are clear, and lightweight managed AWS services ensure operational feasibility for a team of three engineers.
justifications.portability: The architecture cleanly targets AWS eu-west-1 using managed services (Fargate, DynamoDB, S3 Object Lock, EventBridge). While this introduces AWS lock-in, it adheres directly to the requested AWS deployment target.

PERF-01.justification: In-memory caching via ElastiCache, ONNX Runtime, and gRPC support sub-50ms latency. However, synchronous DynamoDB writes and KMS signing in the critical path at 3,000 TPS risk tail latency spikes near the 50 ms P99 target.
sensitivity_points: Network hop latency across API Gateway, scoring engine, and ML inference
Synchronous DynamoDB write and KMS signing overhead during scoring
tradeoffs: Strong audit consistency on critical path vs lower tail latency

PERF-02.justification: Workloads are cleanly separated: case management runs via independent ECS containers, DynamoDB GSIs, and asynchronous EventBridge ingestion, preventing analyst queries from impacting real-time scoring engine resources.
sensitivity_points: DynamoDB read/write capacity allocation between transactional scoring and case queries
tradeoffs: Asynchronous case ingestion via EventBridge vs instantaneous availability in analyst review queues

AVAIL-01.justification: The context defines circuit breaker signals for fail-open fallback back to Payment Gateway/Acquirer systems to avoid blocking transactions. However, internal fallback mechanisms and offline auditing specifics within the engine itself lack detailed component elaboration.
sensitivity_points: Circuit breaker timeout threshold and tripping detection latency
tradeoffs: Failing open to preserve authorization availability vs admitting fraudulent transactions

AVAIL-02.justification: Audit ingestion decouples via DynamoDB Streams, EventBridge, and Firehose into S3 Object Lock, isolating scoring from store degradation. However, synchronous DynamoDB writes and KMS calls in the engine remain a slight bottleneck.
sensitivity_points: Decoupling buffer capacity in EventBridge and DynamoDB Streams
tradeoffs: Asynchronous stream processing preserves latency but risks lag under audit store failures

MOD-01.justification: Dynamic Model Loader and ONNX runtime support runtime swapping without restarts, and telemetry captures model versions. The architecture does not explicitly articulate automated rollback triggers or canary traffic shifting.
sensitivity_points: Dynamic memory reloading speed and thread safety in ONNX runtime
tradeoffs: In-process dynamic model reloading vs rolling container deployments for stability

MOD-02.justification: Rule & Model Management Console and Decision Orchestrator facilitate rule updates, and Explainability Component captures applied rules. Propagation mechanism from Case Management Backend to the Real-Time Scoring Engine is not explicitly detailed.
sensitivity_points: Synchronization latency of active rule configurations across scoring engine replicas
tradeoffs: Dynamic rule distribution complexity vs zero-downtime deployment speed

SEC-01.justification: Tokenization, client-side encryption SDK, sanitizers, and frontend DOM redaction prevent access to PANs. However, automated detection of anomalous analyst access within 15 minutes lacks explicit behavioral anomaly detection components.
sensitivity_points: Strict client-side and API redaction preventing exposure of raw cardholder data
tradeoffs: Tokenization and field-level encryption security vs query flexibility in case management

SEC-02.justification: S3 Object Lock enforces 7-year WORM compliance, AWS KMS provides tamper-evident cryptographic signing, and the Audit Query API with Explainability Component allows retrieval and reproduction of inputs and model attributions within one day.
sensitivity_points: Immutability policies on S3 Object Lock and cryptographic key retention in KMS
tradeoffs: High durability WORM storage cost vs immediate compliance retrieval speed

elements: Real-Time Fraud Screening and Case Management System
